latin: गव्यं वा माहिषं वापि क्षीरं नीरविवर्जितम् । पचेत्स्थाल्यां मृदावग्नौ दर्वीघट्टनसंयुतम् ॥ ६५ ॥ अर्धावशेषं कुर्वीत त्रिभागेनावशेषितम् । षड्भागशेषितं वापि कुर्यादष्टावशेषिकम् ॥ ६६ ॥ अर्धावशिष्टं पाने स्यात्त्रिभागं लेह्यकं भवेत् । षड्भागं पिण्डतामेति शर्करा स्यादथाष्टमे ॥ ६७ ॥
english: Cow's milk, or else buffalo's, free of water — he should cook it in a pot over a soft fire, attended with stirring by a ladle. He should make it half-remaining, or reduced to a third part, or reduced to a sixth part, or he should make it reduced to an eighth. The half-remaining is for drinking; the third part becomes a *lehya*, a thing to be licked; the sixth part goes to the state of a solid lump; and at the eighth it becomes *śarkarā*, sugar.

latin: अर्धावशेषिते दुग्धे तक्रमीषद्विनिक्षिपेत् । नवस्थाल्यां न्यसेत्तत्तु निवाते स्थापयेच्च ताम् ॥ ६८ ॥ शर्करामिश्रितं वापि फलैर्वापि विमिश्रयेत् । यामषट्कोषितं क्षीरमम्लतां घनतां भजेत् ॥ ६९ ॥ दधीति नाम प्राप्नोति पथ्यं मृष्टं मनोहरम् । हीनकाले तथा पथ्यं चिरकालेऽम्लता बहु ॥ १५७० ॥
english: Into milk reduced to a half he should throw a little *takra*. He should set it down in a new pot, and should keep that pot in a windless place. Or it may be mixed with sugar, or he may mix it with fruits as well. Milk left standing six *yāmas* takes on sourness and thickness. It obtains the name *dadhi* — wholesome, sweet, and delightful. In a shorter time it is likewise wholesome; over a long time the sourness is great.

latin: मन्थानेन मथित्वा तन्नवनीतमथो हरेत् । निर्जलं मथितं प्रोक्तमुदस्वित्या(श्विच्च)जलार्धकम् ॥ ७१ ॥ पादाम्बु तक्रमुद्दिष्टं धूपितं हिङ्गुजीरकैः । आर्द्रकेण समायुक्तमेलासैन्धवचूर्णितम् ॥ ७२ ॥
english: Having churned it with a churning-stick, he should then take off the butter. The waterless churned product is declared to be *mathita*; *udaśvit* has half of it water [the edition's own reading here is *udasvityā*, with *udaśvic ca* supplied in the editor's parenthesis; the sense is not in doubt]. That with a quarter part water is designated *takra*. It is fumigated with the smoke of asafoetida and cumin, joined with fresh ginger, and powdered with cardamom and rock salt.
*Mathita* — the undiluted churned curd defined in the previous verse — joined with sugar, mixed with cardamom powder, and fumigated with camphor smoke, is called by the name *majjikā*.

latin: निष्पीड्य दधि वस्त्रेण स्रावयेत्तद्द्रुतं जलम् । शर्करैलासमायुक्ता सूदैः शिखरिणी मता ॥ ७४ ॥
english: Having pressed the *dadhi* in a cloth, he should drain off that water of it quickly. Joined with sugar and cardamom, it is held by cooks to be *śikhariṇī*.

latin: स्रावितं यद्धृतं तोयं जीरकार्द्रकसैन्धवैः । संयुक्तं हिङ्गुधूपेन धूपितं मस्तु कीर्तितम् ॥ ७५ ॥
english: The water that was drained off and kept, joined with cumin, fresh ginger, and rock salt, and fumigated with the smoke of asafoetida, is declared to be *mastu*.

latin: नवनीतं नवं धौतं नीरलेशविवर्जितम् । तापयेदग्निना सम्यक् मृदुना घृतभाण्डके ॥ ७६ ॥ पाके संपूर्णतां याते क्षिपेद्गोधूमबीजकम् । क्षिपेत्ताम्बूलपत्रं च पश्चादुत्तारयेद्घृतम् ॥ ७७ ॥
english: Fresh butter, newly churned, washed, and free of the least trace of water: he should heat it properly over a soft fire in a ghee-pot. When the cooking has gone to completeness, he should throw in a wheat grain; and he should throw in a betel leaf, and afterwards take the ghee off the fire.

latin: तण्डुलक्षालितं तोयं चिञ्चाम्लेन विमिश्रितम् । ईषत्तक्रेण संयुक्तं सितया सह योजितम् ॥ ७८ ॥ एलाचूर्णसमायुक्तमार्द्रकस्य रसेन च । धूपितं हिङ्गुना सम्यक् व्यञ्जनं परिकीर्तितम् ॥ ७९ ॥
english: Water in which rice has been washed, mixed with tamarind sour, joined with a little *takra*, combined with sugar, together with cardamom powder and with the juice of fresh ginger, and thoroughly fumigated with asafoetida: that is declared to be a *vyañjana*.

latin: सौवीरनिर्मलं साम्लं लवणेन च संयुतम् । हिङ्गुना जीरकेणापि धूपितं धूपकाञ्जिकम् ॥ १५८० ॥
english: Clear *sauvīra* — a sour ferment — sour, and joined with salt, fumigated with asafoetida and with cumin as well, is *dhūpa-kāñjika*, the smoked *kāñjika*.

latin: शङ्कुद्वयं समास्थाप्य बध्नीयादुज्ज्वलाम्बरम् । प्रसार्य ष(य)ष्टिभिः किञ्चित्क्षीरमम्लेन भेदितम् ॥ ८१ ॥ सितया च समायुक्तमेलाचूर्णविमिश्रितम् । क्षिपेत्प्रसारिते वस्त्रे स्रावयेत्पेषयेत्समम् ॥ ८२ ॥ पुनः पुनः क्षिपेत्तत्र यावन्निर्मलतां व्रजेत् । पक्वचिञ्चाफलं भृष्टं वर्णार्थं तत्र निक्षिपेत् ॥ ८३ ॥ यस्य कस्य फलस्यापि रसेन परिमिश्रयेत् । तत्तन्नामसमाख्यातं पानकं पेयमुत्तमम् ॥ ८४ ॥
english: Having set two stakes firmly, he should tie a bright cloth to them, spreading it out a little with rods [the edition prints *ṣaṣṭibhiḥ*; *yaṣṭibhiḥ*, "with rods", stands in the editor's parenthesis and is the reading of manuscript A]. Milk split with something sour, joined with sugar and mixed with cardamom powder, he should throw onto the spread cloth; he should let it drain and press it evenly. Again and again he should throw it in there, until it comes clear. Roasted ripe tamarind fruit he should put into it for the sake of colour. He should mix it with the juice of whatever fruit it may be — of this fruit or that. Named after that fruit, it is a *pānaka*, an excellent *peya* [a drink, one of the five classes of food set out at 1344].

latin: सौवर्णे राजते पात्रे रीतियन्त्रविधारिते । भोजयेन्मण्डलेशादीन्यथायोग्यप्रदेशतः ॥ ८५ ॥ विशाले काञ्चने पात्रे स्वर्णकच्चोलसंयुते । लोहगङ्गलकैर्युक्ते रुक्मपिंगालकैर्वृते ॥ ८६ ॥ भंमशुक्तिसमोपेते कनकस्थालसंयुते । जलप्रक्षालिते सम्यक् सितवस्त्रप्रमार्जिते ॥ ८७ ॥ वर्धयेत्पूर्वकथितमन्नपक्वान्नपानकम् । ऊरुनाभिप्रदेशान्तं सञ्छाद्य सितवाससा ॥ ८८ ॥
english: In a golden or a silver vessel held up on a brass frame he should feed the provincial governors and the rest, each from the place appropriate to him. In a broad golden vessel furnished with a golden *kaccola* [a cup; manuscripts A, C, and F read *kambola*], provided with iron *gaṅgalaka*s, ringed about with gold *piṅgālaka*s, supplied with *bhaṃma* [the printed reading; it is not a known word, and a manuscript reads *bhuma*] and shell-shaped spoons, joined with golden platters, thoroughly washed with water and wiped clean with a white cloth — in these he should serve out the boiled rice, the cooked dishes, and the drink described earlier. Having covered himself with a white cloth as far as the region of the thighs and the navel...

latin: गद्दिकायां समासीनः पूर्वाशासम्मुखो नृपः । अन्नं मुद्रसमोपेतं भुञ्जीतोष्णं घृतप्लुतम् ॥ ८९ ॥ प्राचीमुखस्तु भुञ्जान आयुश्च लभते बहु । यशश्च लभतेऽत्यर्थमश्नन्दक्षिणदिङ्मुखः ॥ १५९० ॥ श्रियं तु लभते पुष्टां भुञ्जानः पश्चिमाननः । सत्यवाक्यफलं प्राप्नोत्यश्नन् धनददिङ्मुखः ॥ ९१ ॥
english: ...the king, seated on a cushion with his face towards the eastern quarter, should eat rice hot and flooded with ghee, accompanied by *mudra* [so the edition prints, with no variant recorded; *mudga*, mung bean, is the obvious sense, but it is not what stands in the text]. Eating with his face to the east he obtains long life, and much of it; eating with his face to the southern quarter he obtains fame exceedingly. Eating with his face to the west he obtains prosperity, and it flourishing; eating with his face to the quarter of the giver of wealth — Kubera's north — he obtains the fruit that comes of truthful speech.

latin: श्लक्ष्णमांससमायुक्तं विदलैर्वा विमिश्रितम् । लेहैश्च विविधैर्हृद्यैर्लेपितं वा तथोदनम् ॥ ९२ ॥ मांसप्रकारकैर्मृष्टैरम्लमिश्रैश्च पल्लवैः । नानाविधैस्तथा शाकैः फलपत्रसमुद्भवैः ॥ ९३ ॥ वटकैः पर्पटैर्हृद्यैः खारखण्डोपखण्डकैः । यथारुचि यथासात्म्यं सुखं भुञ्जीत भूपतिः ॥ ९४ ॥
english: And the boiled rice likewise: joined with finely cut meat, or mixed with split pulses, or coated with *leha*s of many kinds and pleasing; with delicious meat preparations of every sort, and with shoots dressed with sour, and likewise with vegetables of many kinds, got from fruits and from leaves; with *vaṭaka*s, with pleasing *parpaṭa*s, and with *khāra-khaṇḍa*s and *upakhaṇḍaka*s [*khāra* is "saline"; the compound looks like salted pieces and lesser pieces, and is not otherwise attested] — the lord of the earth should eat at his ease, according to his liking and according to what agrees with him.

latin: पक्वान्नं पायसं मध्ये शर्कराघृतमिश्रितम् । ततः फलानि भुञ्जीत मधुराम्लरसानि च ॥ ९५ ॥ पिबेच्च पानकं हृद्यं लिह्याच्छिखरिणीमपि । चूषेत मज्जिकां पश्चाद्दधि चाद्याऽत्ततो घनम् ॥ ९६ ॥ ततस्तक्रान्नमश्नीयात्सैन्धवेन च संयुतम् । क्षीरं वापि पिबेत्पश्चात्पिबेद्वा काञ्जिकं वरम् ॥ ९७ ॥
english: In the middle of the meal, a cooked dish and a *pāyasa* mixed with sugar and ghee. Then he should eat fruits, and those sweet and sour in their juice. And he should *drink* a pleasing *pānaka*; he should *lick* the *śikhariṇī* as well; afterwards he should *suck* the *majjikā*; and he should eat *dadhi*, and after that the thickened milk. [The three verbs — *pibet*, *lihyāt*, *cūṣeta* — are the verbs of the fivefold classification of food announced at 1344, *bhojya*, *bhakṣya*, *peya*, *lehya*, *coṣya*: the close of the meal runs through the classes in their own order.] Then he should eat *takra*-rice, joined with rock salt; or afterwards he should drink milk, or else he should drink excellent *kāñjika*.

latin: मांसमम्लेन भुञ्जीत दुग्धं वा शर्करायुतम् । लवणेन तथा चाम्लं क्षारं कटुकषायकैः ॥ ९८ ॥ वसन्ते कटु चाश्नीयाद्ग्रीष्मे मधुरशीतलम् । वर्षासु च तथा क्षारं मधुरं शरदि स्मृतम् ॥ ९९ ॥ हेमन्ते स्निग्धमुष्णं च शिशिरेऽप्युष्णमम्लकम् । एवं भुञ्जीत यद्भूपो अन्नभोगः स कथ्यते ॥ १६०० ॥ अन्नभोगः समाख्यातः सोमेश्वरमहीभुजा । ॥ इत्यन्नभोगः ॥ १३ ॥
english: He should eat meat with something sour, or milk joined with sugar [manuscripts D and F read *śarkarayā saha*, "together with sugar"]; and what is sour with salt, and what is alkaline with pungent and astringent things. In spring he should eat what is pungent; in summer, what is sweet and cooling; in the rains, likewise what is alkaline; in autumn, sweet is prescribed. In early winter, what is unctuous and hot; in late winter too, what is hot and sour. That which a king eats in this manner is called the Enjoyment of Food. The Enjoyment of Food has been set forth by Someśvara, lord of the earth. Thus the Enjoyment of Food. 13.
